title: Probe initial warmup latency caused underscale during regional traffic surge (postmortem)
creator: Priya Nair
description: During a regional traffic surge on 2026-02-28 we experienced sustained underprovisioning for the guest-model serving pool in eu-west-1. The immediate symptom was elevated request latency and queueing without the usual autoscaler response; downstream services reported 5–10s tail latencies and a 12% increase in 429s for bursty endpoints. This document captures timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations performed during the incident, and recommended action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-28 09:02 UTC: Synthetic traffic spike from partner integration begins.
2026-02-28 09:05 UTC: Service X latency climbs - alerts (latency SLO breach) fire.
2026-02-28 09:06 UTC: Initial ops triage: pods at 100% CPU but HPA/KEDA did not scale as expected.
2026-02-28 09:10 UTC: Investigation shows KEDA trigger metrics delayed ~45s due to aggregator TTL and probe warmup smoothing.
2026-02-28 09:14 UTC: Manual scale up performed to stabilize latency (hotfix).
2026-02-28 10:00 UTC: Traffic recedes; system returns to baseline.
2026-03-01: Post-incident deep-dive started.
2026-03-03: Reproduced underprovisioning in a staged cluster with synthetic burst tests.
2026-03-05: Drafted proposed fixes and temporary mitigations; PR opened to increase KEDA polling frequency and add warmup window.
2026-03-07: Postmortem draft ready for review.
impact_summary: Customer-facing impact was moderate-to-high: multiple customers observed increased tail latency and elevated 429s for routed LLM inference requests in eu-west-1 for ~8 minutes while manual remediation was applied. No data loss. Estimated affected request volume: ~120k requests; error uplift ~12% during the peak window. Internal SLO breach recorded and incident escalated to Eng+SRE.
root_cause: The autoscaler relied on a percentile-based metric aggregation pipeline that included a 30s TTL/buffer and a 1-minute smoothing window to reduce noise. Combined with a recent change to readiness probe behavior (initialDelaySeconds increased to 10 to mitigate false evictions), the KEDA trigger experienced delayed and smoothed signals during a short, high-intensity spike. This produced a false negative—KEDA did not perceive the spike magnitude quickly enough to scale, leading to undersubscription of serving capacity. A secondary contributor was a recent metrics transport optimization that batched metrics with an extra 20–40s flush in low-traffic conditions, increasing end-to-end metric latency.
contributing_factors: KEDA scaler configured with conservative polling interval (60s) after prior noise-driven flaps
Percentile smoothing window (60s) aggregated away short-duration spikes
Readiness probe initialDelaySeconds increased in 2026-02-15 deploy, slowing pod available-to-serve transition
Metrics pipeline batching/TTL optimization introduced extra 20–40s latency for trigger metrics
No synthetic spike tests covering sub-60s bursts in the autoscaling test harness
mitigations_taken: Manually increased replica count in eu-west-1 serving pool to absorb traffic (hotfix) - 2026-02-28 09:14 UTC
Temporarily reverted the most recent metric-batching optimization in staging to verify impact
Opened PR to reduce KEDA polling interval from 60s to 15s during daytime business hours (PR #2589)
Short-term adjustment: add detector for rapid ingress rate change to trigger immediate scale (feature-flagged)
Raised alerts for 'scaler-unresponsive' when request latency increases but scaler metrics show flatness
long_term_actions: Implement a KEDA warmup window config: allow scaler to apply aggressive scale-up for first 30s of detected bursts
Refactor metrics pipeline to provide low-latency path for autoscaling triggers (remove batching for trigger metrics)
Add sub-60s burst tests to the autoscaling CI harness and include them in pre-release gates
Re-evaluate readiness/readiness probe trade-offs and document safe ranges for initialDelaySeconds across different instance types
Create a runbook for autoscaler false-negative incidents with clear playbook for immediate mitigations

notes: This incident surfaced a classic trade-off between noise suppression and responsiveness. Several earlier changes (intended to reduce flapping) aligned in an adverse way for short, intense bursts. The recommended pattern is to maintain a separate, low-latency signal path for scaling decisions and to keep smoothing/percentile logic for non-critical analytics only. Reviewers: SRE, Serving Runtime, Observability leads.
